title: The Link That Must Fire, and How to Put It Back

scenes.visual: Title card: The Link That Must Fire.

scenes.tts: Which molecule turns the calcium signal into release at this synapse?
scenes.visual: A ribbon synapse with calcium entering and a question mark over the fusion step.
scenes.narration: Which molecule turns the calcium signal into release at this synapse?

scenes.tts: When an inner hair cell depolarizes, calcium enters. Something must turn that signal into vesicle fusion.
scenes.visual: Calcium channels open at the active zone; vesicles sit by the ribbon, not yet fusing.
scenes.narration: When an inner hair cell depolarizes, calcium enters. Something must turn that signal into vesicle fusion.

scenes.tts: The ribbon is not that something. It keeps a larger resident pool of vesicles.
scenes.visual: The ribbon highlighted with its vesicle pool, labelled supply, not trigger.
scenes.narration: The ribbon is not that something. It keeps a larger resident pool of vesicles.

scenes.tts: Mutations in the otoferlin gene cause deafness, and otoferlin carries calcium-binding C two domains.
scenes.caption: Mutations in the OTOF gene cause deafness, and otoferlin carries calcium-binding C2 domains.
scenes.visual: A gene diagram with a mutation marker, beside the protein drawn as labelled domains binding calcium. On screen: OTOF, C2 domains.
scenes.narration: Mutations in the OTOF gene cause deafness, and otoferlin carries calcium-binding C2 domains.

scenes.tts: Roux and colleagues recorded from inner hair cells of mice lacking otoferlin.
scenes.visual: A pipette on one inner hair cell. On screen: Roux and colleagues, 2006; Otof-null mice.
scenes.narration: Roux and colleagues recorded from inner hair cells of mice lacking otoferlin.

scenes.tts: A rise in membrane capacitance tracks how much vesicle membrane fused. So it measures release.
scenes.visual: A capacitance trace stepping up as vesicles fuse in a control cell.
scenes.narration: A rise in membrane capacitance tracks how much vesicle membrane fused. So it measures release.

scenes.tts: If otoferlin acts after calcium enters, at fusion itself, what should the recording show?
scenes.visual: Two blank traces labelled calcium current and capacitance, with question marks.
scenes.narration: If otoferlin acts after calcium enters, at fusion itself, what should the recording show?

scenes.visual: Hold on the blank traces.

scenes.tts: Calcium current and ribbon morphogenesis were preserved at the age recorded. Release was almost abolished.
scenes.visual: The calcium current trace fills in as normal; the capacitance trace stays flat. The ribbon is drawn intact.
scenes.narration: Calcium current and ribbon morphogenesis were preserved at the age recorded. Release was almost abolished.

scenes.tts: They proposed that otoferlin may be the major calcium sensor for fusion. The word may mattered.
scenes.visual: A sensor label with a dashed outline and the word may in italics.
scenes.narration: They proposed that otoferlin may be the major calcium sensor for fusion. The word may mattered.

scenes.tts: A knockout shows a protein is needed. It does not show the protein is the sensor.
scenes.visual: Two cards: needed, and is the sensor, with the second marked not yet shown.
scenes.narration: A knockout shows a protein is needed. It does not show the protein is the sensor.

scenes.tts: Michalski and colleagues made a sharper test. A change in the C two C domain reduced calcium binding.
scenes.caption: Michalski and colleagues made a sharper test. A change in the C2C domain reduced calcium binding.
scenes.visual: The protein with one domain marked and fewer calcium ions bound. On screen: Michalski and colleagues, 2017.
scenes.narration: Michalski and colleagues made a sharper test. A change in the C2C domain reduced calcium binding.

scenes.tts: The calcium sensitivity of release fell, which fits a sensing role, without making otoferlin the only sensor.
scenes.visual: Two release curves, the knock-in shifted so more calcium is needed, with a second dashed question-mark sensor beside the label.
scenes.narration: The calcium sensitivity of release fell, which fits a sensing role, without making otoferlin the only sensor.

scenes.tts: Now the repair. In severe otoferlin deafness, the inner hair cells are there to treat, but their synapses release almost nothing.
scenes.visual: The chain of three links: the inner hair cell drawn present as the treatment target, its synapse dim with vesicles that do not fuse, and one or two ribbons faded, so the drawing does not imply every synapse is intact.
scenes.narration: Now the repair. In severe otoferlin deafness, the inner hair cells are there to treat, but their synapses release almost nothing.

scenes.tts: The outer hair cells still amplify, at least early in life. The ear's own faint sounds, otoacoustic emissions, show it.
scenes.visual: Outer hair cells drawn working, with a small sound wave leaving the ear. Label: otoacoustic emissions present.
scenes.narration: The outer hair cells still amplify, at least early in life. The ear's own faint sounds, otoacoustic emissions, show it.

scenes.tts: But the gene is too large for its vector. A conventional adeno-associated virus carries about five kilobases.
scenes.visual: A vector drawn as a small suitcase. On screen: about 4.7 to 5 kb capacity.
scenes.narration: But the gene is too large for its vector. A conventional adeno-associated virus carries about five kilobases.

scenes.tts: The otoferlin coding sequence is about six kilobases, before a promoter is added.
scenes.visual: A gene bar overflowing the suitcase. On screen: about 6 kb.
scenes.narration: The otoferlin coding sequence is about six kilobases, before a promoter is added.

scenes.tts: So Al-Moyed and colleagues split it between two vectors. A cell receiving both can rebuild the full gene.
scenes.visual: The bar cut in two, each half loaded into a differently coloured vector, rejoining inside one cell. On screen: Al-Moyed and colleagues, 2019.
scenes.narration: So Al-Moyed and colleagues split it between two vectors. A cell receiving both can rebuild the full gene.

scenes.tts: If each vector independently reaches seventy percent of hair cells, what fraction can make the protein?
scenes.visual: A row of hair cells, some marked with one colour, some with the other, some with both. On screen: each vector 70 percent.
scenes.narration: If each vector independently reaches seventy percent of hair cells, what fraction can make the protein?

scenes.visual: Hold on the row of hair cells.

scenes.tts: About half, because a cell needs both halves to rebuild the gene.
scenes.visual: Only the cells carrying both colours turn gold. On screen: 0.7 times 0.7 equals 0.49.
scenes.narration: About half, because a cell needs both halves to rebuild the gene.

scenes.tts: The real mice are a separate question. Full-length otoferlin appeared in up to half their inner hair cells.
scenes.visual: A new panel, labelled real mice: a row of inner hair cells with up to half of them gold. On screen: up to 50 percent.
scenes.narration: The real mice are a separate question. Full-length otoferlin appeared in up to half their inner hair cells.

scenes.tts: Fast release came back in those cells. Vesicle replenishment reached only part of wild-type values.
scenes.visual: A capacitance trace with a restored fast step and a shallower later slope. On screen: replenishment 35 to 50 percent of wild type.
scenes.narration: Fast release came back in those cells. Vesicle replenishment reached only part of wild-type values.

scenes.tts: Treated mice had click thresholds of forty to sixty decibels. That is partial rescue, not normal hearing.
scenes.caption: Treated mice had click thresholds of 40 to 60 dB SPL. That is partial rescue, not normal hearing.
scenes.visual: A threshold scale with the treated range marked well above the wild-type range.
scenes.narration: Treated mice had click thresholds of 40 to 60 dB SPL. That is partial rescue, not normal hearing.

scenes.tts: Replacing a missing link can work because the cells that need it are still alive.
scenes.visual: Final card: the chain with the middle link restored inside a living cell.
scenes.narration: Replacing a missing link can work because the cells that need it are still alive.

scenes.visual: End card: The Link That Must Fire.
